slides: PRICE YOUR FIRST DIGITAL SERVICE
Start with scope. Then calculate your cost.
Price the work clearly.

DEFINE THE DELIVERABLE
What will you make? How many revisions? When is it due?
Make the scope specific.
creator holding checklist, three blue and orange deliverable cards
CALCULATE YOUR BASE
Hours × your rate + direct costs. This gives you a starting point.
Know your cost first.

SHOW ONE CLEAR PACKAGE
List the result, timeline, price and what is included.
Make the offer easy to read.

Agree on a price before adding anything outside the scope.
Set boundaries early.

STOP POSTING RANDOMLY
Choose three content pillars your audience can recognise.
Build a clear content system.

Who are you helping? What problem do they want to solve?
Know who the post is for.

Share one useful lesson, checklist or simple walkthrough.
Make one thing easier.

Show the work behind the result.

Document your learning.

posts.topic: Use AI for notes without copying
slides: USE AI FOR NOTES WITHOUT COPYING
Turn your own material into questions, not ready-made answers.
Use AI to support learning.
student creator studying beside notes and blue AI assistant icon
START WITH YOUR MATERIAL
Use your class notes or allowed source. Remove private details.
Give the tool useful context.
creator feeding notebook pages into laptop
ASK FOR A CLEAR OUTLINE
Group the key ideas. Flag anything that needs checking.
Organise before you memorise.
creator arranging three organised folders
REWRITE IN YOUR OWN WORDS
Close the AI answer. Explain the concept from memory.
Understanding beats copying.
creator writing in notebook with closed laptop
CHECK THE ORIGINAL SOURCE
Verify facts, formulas and citations. Fix any errors.
Treat AI output as a draft.
creator checking book with magnifying glass
TEST YOURSELF TODAY
Ask for five practice questions. Answer first, then review.
Save this + try active recall.
creator holding quiz cards and a notebook

posts.topic: Small business systems that save daily time
slides: SAVE TIME WITH SIMPLE SYSTEMS
Give repeat tasks a clear place, owner and next step.
Make daily work easier.
creator organising blue and orange workflow trays
CAPTURE EVERY REQUEST
Keep orders and enquiries in one shared tracker.
Stop losing work in chats.
creator collecting message cards into one inbox
TRACK THE NEXT ACTION
Add an owner, due date and status for each task.
Make the next move visible.
creator pointing to compact task board
SAVE REUSABLE REPLIES
Prepare answers for common questions. Check details before sending.
Reply faster with care.
creator holding blue response cards beside laptop
USE A DAILY CHECKLIST
Check pending orders, payments and follow-ups at the end of the day.
Close the open loops.
creator ticking notebook checklist
IMPROVE ONE REPEAT TASK
Choose one weekly bottleneck. Test a simpler process for seven days.
Save this + simplify one task.
creator moving a process card through a small gear

posts.topic: Turn templates into a digital product
slides: TURN A TEMPLATE INTO A PRODUCT
Start with one repeat problem you already know how to solve.
Useful comes before fancy.
creator presenting orange template package
CHOOSE ONE SPECIFIC USER
A student, freelancer or shop owner needs different tools.
Build for one clear need.
creator choosing one blue user card
BUILD A SMALL FIRST VERSION
Make one reusable template that solves one task well.
Keep the first version focused.
creator designing neat template sheet on laptop
ADD A WORKED EXAMPLE
Include instructions and sample data so the buyer can get started.
Make it easy to use.
creator holding instruction card and completed example
TEST IT WITH REAL USERS
Ask a few people to try it. Fix the confusing steps.
Let feedback shape the product.
creator reviewing feedback cards
WRITE AN HONEST PRODUCT PAGE
Show what is included, who it helps and its limits.
Save this + build one useful file.
creator showing product page on laptop beside template box

posts.topic: Build a small tool instead of watching tutorials
slides: BUILD ONE SMALL TOOL
Choose a real task. Make a simple version that works.
Learn by finishing.
creator assembling blue tool blocks beside laptop
PICK A TINY PROBLEM
Try a task timer, expense tracker or reusable checklist.
Keep the first goal small.
creator choosing among timer, calculator and checklist props
DEFINE WHAT DONE MEANS
Write three features. Leave the extras for later.
Give the project a finish line.
creator showing three feature cards and finish flag
LEARN ONLY THE NEXT STEP
Find the lesson you need. Apply it in your project immediately.
Turn learning into action.
creator transferring book concept to laptop project
TEST THE MAIN FLOW
Try normal input, empty input and a mistake. Fix what breaks.
Make the basic path reliable.
creator checking laptop beside three test cards
SHIP AND SHOW YOUR WORK
Share a demo, explain the problem and note one improvement.
Save this + finish your first tool.
creator presenting finished laptop app with small launch rocket

posts.topic: AI study tools with a clear workflow
slides: BUILD A SMARTER STUDY SYSTEM
Give each AI task a clear purpose. Keep the learning your own.
Build a workflow you can repeat.
creator with organised study book and blue AI helper icon
PLAN ONE STUDY SESSION
Choose a topic, time limit and one thing you want to understand.
Start with a clear goal.
creator pointing to topic card and timer
ASK FOR A SIMPLE EXPLANATION
Request a short example. Compare it with your course material.
Check before you trust.
creator comparing book and blue explanation card
GENERATE PRACTICE QUESTIONS
Ask for questions at your level. Attempt them before seeing answers.
Practise before you review.
creator sorting quiz cards beside laptop
REVIEW YOUR MISTAKES

Turn mistakes into useful notes.
creator reviewing notebook and correction cards
REPEAT FOR SEVEN DAYS
Track one focused session each day. Review what you can recall.
Save this + study with purpose.
